articleTitle: Prediction of Gestational Diabetes by Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Diabetes is the most common noncommunicable disease among people in the world due to changes in food habits. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is most frequently found in women after the birth of a baby. This article describes the prediction of GDM with various machine learning (ML) algorithms demonstrated on the Polyisocyanurate Insulation Manufacturers Association (PIMA) data set. The accuracy of various ML algorithms is validated with metrics. The significance of ML algorithms is demonstrated using a confusion matrix as well as receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and area under the curve (AUC) scores in handling the diabetes PIMA data set.

articleTitle: Security Analysis of an Automobile Controller Area Network Bus
abstract: As vehicles added more complex electrical systems, point-to-point electrical wiring became heavy and expensive. In 1986, the Society of Automotive Engineers proposed the first in-vehicle network, referred to as the controller area network (CAN) (Corrigan 2008). The proposed network was envisioned as a simple network to reduce wiring and allow multiple microcontrollers to communicate on a single bus.

articleTitle: Velocity Measurement in Automotive Sensing: How FMCW Radar and Lidar Can Work Together
abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) depend on an intricate network of camera, radar, lidar, and inertial sensors to navigate safely. Discussing the merits and drawbacks of individual sensors is one of the more consistent "water-cooler topics" in the autonomous driving industry. Although this sensor face-off is entertaining, it is sometimes more useful to consider how two sensors can work together. I will discuss two sensors that can directly sense velocity in the context of future AV capability.

articleTitle: Examining the Sensors That Enable Self-Driving Vehicles
abstract: There is a lot of buzz regarding the automobile industry, and the dominant goal for car manufacturers is to enhance drivers' experiences. Engine optimization and alternative fuels have made progress toward their full potential; so the next step is creating self-driving vehicles. The first group to explore this idea was DARPA in the early 2000s. Since 2010, major technological advancements have been achieved. As crazy as it may sound, self-driving vehicles are being developed, and research funding has shifted toward this goal. The future is coming, and within the next decade, the first commercial prototypes are expected to be available for mass use.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Handling Big Data for Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: The tremendous advancement in information and communication technology (ICT) has led to the rise of a hot topic: "big data." Big data is defined as large data sets that are complex and, as a result, cannot be handled by traditional methods. Among the many contributors to big data are largescale and densely distributed wireless sensor networks (WSNs), which pose a number of challenges that must be resolved in parallel.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks: Alternate Drivers' Visual Perception
abstract: The number of U.S. states considering legislation related to autonomous vehicles has increased in the past few years, and a truck without a cab or driver was recently test-driven in Sweden. These self-driving vehicles would not have emerged without the advent of artificial-intelligence technologies and their success with everyday problems. A crucial task in autonomous driving is providing a substitute for human visual perception of the routes and surroundings so that the vehicle can operate by itself. This task primarily involves image classification-that is, automatically assigning a category label, such as a pedestrian, lane marking, or pothole, to a photo captured by a vehicle's camera sensors, which is the focus of this article.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Pipelines: From Research to Production
abstract: Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) are getting lot of attention these days, and an increasing number of people are interested in becoming data scientists. Many imagine ML/AI as a black box that does its magic and is somehow able to make predictions. Well, the magic is that an ML algorithm is designed in such a way that it is able to find a pattern in data that have the correct answers and use that to predict the next answer. The learning task may vary from predicting the next word in a sentence, a sentiment, or what else would you like to buy based on what you already have in your basket.

articleTitle: Nanonetworks and Molecular Communications for Biomedical Applications
abstract: For millions of years, cells have evolved to perform incredible functions in all living organisms despite their nanoscale size. Consider white blood cells. They are fighting a never-ending war against bacteria, viruses, and other threats that enter your body. They produce vital antibodies to destroy pathogens in ways that almost seem as if the cells are independently communicating. And yes, this is true: cells do communicate, typically through the release of chemical compounds that trigger responses in nearby cells. To give a specific example related to white blood cells, basophils (a type of white blood cell) release histamines, which prompt blood vessels to dilate near the affected area of the body. This increases blood flow to the region, allowing for more white blood cells to reach the area and at tack suspected pathogens nearby.

articleTitle: Data: The New Form of Wealth and Power
abstract: Footsteps in the sands of time were made by exploring the new, the unknown, and the mysterious; discovering the secrets of the universe; and exploiting its resources. Over time, humans traveled to the moon, discovered fire, and used raw materials to invent machines to ease their lives. The current century is witnessing a technological revolution: people have started to use smartphones, smartwatches, drones, and connected Internet of Things (IoT) devices, among other technologies. What is interesting about this technological advancement is the fact that all invented devices share a common raw material: data.

articleTitle: Do You Call That a Lab Notebook?
abstract: "Electronic laboratory notebooks (ELNs)? What are those?" At the start of every academic year, I prepare myself for a battle with my third-year engineering students about laboratory notebooks. More often than not, they either hand me a neatly written diary or loose bits of paper that are half folded and randomly glued to the back cover of a jotter. At first, my students dismiss the idea of keeping a properly documented lab notebook, but I notice a change in attitude when they are introduced to electronic notebooks.

articleTitle: VetLink: A Livestock Disease-Management System
abstract: Diagnosing, preventing, and treating animal diseases have always been important issues for the livestock industry. Having the ability to receive timely information pertaining to their sick animals is extremely useful for livestock producers, who usually live in rural areas where it is difficult to get immediate access to a veterinarian. Advances in technology have made it possible to improve human health care through e-health approaches, such as the popular website WebMD. A similar tactic could be borrowed to enhance and improve veterinary care for farmers in the livestock industry.

articleTitle: The Autonomous Mobility Innovation Lifecycle
abstract: The driverless future promised by next-generation mobility will be made possible by two new technologies: on-demand mobility services, such as ride-hailing and last-mile delivery, and autonomous vehicles (AVs), which can be used for consumer transportation and logistics. An innovation and its adoption advance along a fourphase lifecycle, and we can evaluate the performance of these two driverless mobility technologies using distinct progressions. This article presents an analysis of the AV innovation lifecycle and introduces four dimensions by which to measure its performance over time. Finally, it reveals five requirements that must be addressed before AV use can be scaled for consumer transportation and logistics.

articleTitle: The Rise of Android Banking Trojans
abstract: As soon as banks began developing mobile applications to enable users to perform financial activities online, cybercriminals started formulating ways to penetrate this new channel and perform illicit transactions. For criminals, it is easier to exploit the scarce end-user security awareness and attack individual clients' devices rather than directly target the portals of banks.

articleTitle: How Genetic Sequence Data Can Guide Vaccine Design
abstract: Vaccines have saved more lives than any other medical intervention throughout human history by preventing the spread of infectious diseases. Experts credit vaccines with preventing an estimated 6 million annual deaths worldwide. Perhaps the greatest vaccine success story is that of the eradication of the smallpox disease, which is believed to have killed approximately 300 million people between 1900 and 1977, while disfiguring and blinding millions more. For perspective, that is more lives lost than the combined death toll of both world wars.

articleTitle: Building a Low-Cost Weather Station
abstract: The study and construction of a low-cost weather station emerged from a scientific initiation project, "Modeling and Analysis of a Wind-Photovoltaic Hybrid System With the Application of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator in Urban Areas," developed at the Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF). During the initial stages of this project, there was a need to understand the climate data, which influence the development and proper functioning of wind and photovoltaic systems. However, buying or having access to such measuring equipment requires a high investment. As a result, we sought to collect data related to wind generation and solar photovoltaic energy, such as wind speed, irradiance, temperature, and air humidity, by constructing a low-cost weather station with an Arduino Uno board, electronic sensors, and data storage in a memory card.

articleTitle: Connected, Autonomous Cars: Passive Pothole Patrollers
abstract: In November 2018, I was driving on the highway at night in upstate New York. The blowing snow and sleet made it difficult to see far ahead, but I noticed several cars pulled over on the side of the road with their hazard lights f lashing. Assuming they had been in an accident, I pulled into the left lane when I suddenly struck an invisible obstacle, blowing my tires. After reaching safe location, I called 911 to relay what little information I could recall. I didn?t know what I had hit or even where it was. That evening, half a dozen motorists struck the same hazard before authorities arrived on the scene.

articleTitle: Design of DNA Digital Circuits
abstract: Digital logic is taught globally in almost all engineering schools. The subject consists of elementary knowledge of Boolean algebra, simple logic gates, and design of an elementary computer. With the help of AND, OR, and NOT, we can make any digital circuit. Recently, there has been increasing interest in the creation of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) logic gates due to forthcoming applications in the medical field. This article explains elementary ideas about AND, OR and NOT gates based on DNA-strand displacement. Once these gates are made, the path to developing any DNA digital circuit becomes open. DNA gates can be used for both DNA logic circuits and DNA computers. In this article, we provide the fundamentals of DNA circuits with possible applications.

articleTitle: Advancing Technology for a Healthier Humanity
abstract: Medical technology (MedTech) includes the products, services, or solutions that aim at improving survival and quality of life. These technologies can include preventive, diagnostic, or therapeutic technologies. Key technologies in this space include medical devices, in vitro diagnostics, medical imaging, prosthetics and orthotics, medical signal processing, health informatics and communications technologies, wearables, medical robotics, and regenerative medicine. According to the IQVIA's "The Rise of Global Medical Technology" report, MedTech worldwide is an extremely valuable market, with an estimated global revenue of US$438 billion in 2017. This is a fast-growing industry, with a compound annual growth rate of 6%, and it is estimated to reach US$585 billion in 2022.

articleTitle: Data Architecture: A Sustainable Foundation for Data Exploitation
abstract: Many of companies have launched digital transformation programs. Such programs must support the evolution of businesses toward the digital age. Data and their exploitation are at the core of these transformation programs. The ability to use, explore, and analyze data as well as create value within a short time to market are becoming major challenges.

articleTitle: Playing Fair With Time Series Data
abstract: Data graphics had to be invented: The idea of using diagrams to represent numerical data emerged only toward the end of the 18th century. While graphs of mathematical functions existed before this time, it fell to a Scottish scoundrel, William Playfair, to popularize the idea of graphically representing empirical data in all of their messiness.

articleTitle: Multidisciplinary Expertise for Exploration Medical System Design
abstract: The design of exploration class missions that send crews beyond low-Earth orbit has uncovered challenging crew health and performance (CHP) needs not previously faced in human spacef light. The engineers who design and build the medical systems integrated into a habitat and the clinicians who ultimately use those systems to provide care to astronauts must work together with a common language and design processes to effectively address such needs. This article proposes adapting systems engineering tools to provide a streamlined, thorough, and efficient method for communicating between clinical and engineering disciplines to advance human health and performance in space.

articleTitle: Air-Leak Localization in Pressurized Space Structures
abstract: Micrometeoroid and orbital debris (MMOD) are the leading cause of damage to space structures, such as the International Space Station (ISS). These tiny particles, with a diameter of less than 25-125 mm and traveling at hypervelocity from 7 to 10 km/s, can cause severe damage and start an air leak (Fig. 1). Fast and accurate localization of air leaks is critical for space exploration. This article outlines the process of basic and applied research that led to solving the leak localization problem. The developed prototype was flight certified and tested onboard the ISS.

articleTitle: Synthetic Biology: What's In It for Electrical Engineers?
abstract: On the surface, electrical engineering and the genetic engineering of bacteria may appear to be disparate fields with little in common. The former concerns the assembly of electronic components to build systems that sense and compute in the electrical domain. Bacterial genetic engineering, on the other hand, involves modifying the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) of bacterial cells to arrive at organisms that have new, altered behavior.

articleTitle: When Digital Technologies Rule the Lecture Theater
abstract: The proliferation of digital technologies in education is leading to a new academic era that is both chaotic and opportunistic. The educational landscape is evolving-and so are staff and students-to meet tomorrow's challenges and needs, including curricula, mindsets, environments, and tools.

articleTitle: Driving Toward New Mobility
abstract: We are proud to bring to you an issue focused on a pertinent topic-new mobility. The term new mobility was coined to represent four pivotal technologies that will change how we move not only ourselves but also our cargo: connected cars, autonomy, shared mobility, and electrification. The acronyms CASE or ACES are often used to convey these traits that new mobility entails.

articleTitle: Recent Machine Learning Applications in Space
abstract: The many terabytes of data that are generated from space missions must be analyzed, and accurate decisions must be made. This article highlights two important areas where automated machine learning (ML) systems are helping to science the data and allowing engineers and scientists to make more informed decisions without drowning in ones and zeros. One such area is exoplanet detection. This application is particularly unique because data analysis is crowdsourced as part of a citizen science effort in which members of the public who are not part of the science team take part, using powerful open source methods and software tools running on clusters of servers available in the cloud.

articleTitle: Battle of the Rockets
abstract: The team of nine students from the Virginia Military Institute (VMI) collectively held their breath during the countdown. The result of their yearlong project-an 11-fttall, 60-lb rocket-stood on the launchpad, holding an autonomous soil-collecting robot they had designed. There was little doubt the engines would ignite, developing 450 lbf of thrust within 200 ms; their worry was whether the robot would eject at apogee and survive the resulting 1,000-ft fall. These were the opening minutes of the Battle of the Rockets Competition, hosted by the Federation of Galaxy Explorers, in Culpepper, Virginia. in April 2019. The competition allows high school and college students to enter different contests of varying degrees of difficulty that test their skills in rocket and robot design. There are three different contests; in order of complexity, they are the Target Altitude, Sounding Rocket, and Mars Rover events. This article describes the VMI's entry in the Mars Rover event, which involves designing an autonomous robot launched from a rocket. No teams have fully completed all facets of the Mars Rover challenge since the rules were made more stringent in 2015.

articleTitle: Applied Machine Learning Strategies
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning (ML), fueled by new frameworks and algorithms, more powerful computing architectures, scalable cloud-based services, and availability of large-scale data sets, have enabled scientists and engineers to tackle more complex problems than ever before. Computer hardware has made tremendous leaps in processing power, bit depth, caching, and storage. Graphics processing units, developed originally for the gaming industry, provide a parallel processing capability that is ideally suited to computer vision (CV) and the simulation of artificial neural networks. The expansion to cloud-based services allows researchers virtually unlimited scaling of resources to tackle problems having millions of input attributes, with output domains up to thousands of potentially nonexclusive classes.

articleTitle: Traveled Earth, Learned About Space
abstract: Dreaming of space travel is increasingly common. There are so many science fiction movies and TV shows, popular songs, and space observation centers for people of all ages-even science-themed fashion fuels our curiosity. These ventures were first inspired by the results of pioneering space programs in the 1950s-1970s. In chronological order, the early programs in the United States were the <;i>Freedom Seven<;/i> (1961, one astronauts per vehicle), Gemini (1961-1966, two astronauts per vehicle), and <;i>Apollo<;/i> missions (1963-1972, with three astronauts per vehicle, which led to the first human moon landing in 1969) as well as the <;i>Skylab<;/i> program (1973-1974), which launched the first U.S. space station. Other achievements from that era included the launch of the <;i>Sputnik, Vostok<;/i>, and <;i>Luna<;/i> spacecraft as part of the Soviet space program.

articleTitle: Why Aren't Embedded Fuel-Quality Sensors in Our Cars?
abstract: Sensor-based systems are expanding rapidly. Countless sensors are unceasingly taking measures around us. Embedded with other electronics, they create automated systems designed to improve the performance and reliability of equipment and devices. The automotive industry has applied an increasing number of sensors to different parts of vehicles. Numerous applications range from alarms and multimedia to the sensors that control temperature and combustion timing, guaranteeing safety, fuel-consumption efficiency, and comfort.

articleTitle: The Case Against Autonomous Cars
abstract: There is a lot of interest in autonomous cars. The hype tells us that "in just a few years" autonomous vehicles will be able to be driven on any road. They will be commercially available in five years, said Google founder Sergey Brin in 2012, and in Norway, the minister of transportation explained that there is no need to regulate Uber as we will have driverless taxies in a few years. All of this seems very promising.

articleTitle: Beyond Marie Curie: Grace Hopper and the ENIAC Six
abstract: I recently went to lunch with some friends, and we ended up discussing the lack of female role models in engineering and how that may be limiting the growth of diversity in our field. The discussion went a little further, and the point was made that the role models we already have are not getting enough attention.

articleTitle: Designing a Respiratory-Rate Monitor for Developing Countries
abstract: The health-care systems in developing countries struggle due to lack of proper resources, insufficient staff, and inadequate training. This means thousands of people are without adequate treatment and can be improperly diagnosed. Vital signs are fundamental tools that doctors use for diagnosis, so it is necessary to have equipment that can monitor them over time.

articleTitle: It Takes More Than Technologies
abstract: Eura Nova was built in 2008 on a wave of new technologies that were to revolutionize the world, and its mission was to boost this revolution in Europe. We created Eura Nova to give a competitive advantage to companies thanks to cutting-edge IT technology. How? First, by combining three kinds of expertise: data science, data architecture, and software development. All three are articulated: data science models' full potential can be unleashed if and when they are supported by an architecture that makes the digital shift possible and when they are applied in a user-friendly solution developed wisely in the client company's technical environment. Second, by using a one-of-a-kind business model, as Eura Nova is a consultancy company supported by a product incubator and a private research center. To perform scientific research in computer science meant studying the new landscape of distributed computing architectures and leveraging their power with machine learning algorithms applied on large amounts of data, which requires a lot of calculation power.

articleTitle: My Learning Journey in a Data Company
abstract: After I graduated with a Ph.D. degree in French literature, I did not know what I wanted to do with my life. Sure, I would have loved to use everything I had learned during my studies or continue with an academic career, but jobs were scarce, and the competitors were far more upstart than I. At that time, I spotted a company that was looking for an external relations officer for which no specific degree was required; social and speaking skills were the best assets to have. Well, they also specified that candidates should be interested in new information technologies ... which I definitely was not. Still, I sent my curriculum vitae (CV)-the paper version, because that's what someone with a Ph.D. degree in literature does.

articleTitle: The Importance of Advisor-Advisee Relationships in Graduate School
abstract: Have you ever felt uneasy in a relationship, but you could not figure out the exact problem? My advisor was quiet and passive for a while, and he kept hiding his concerns until I met with him to fill out my annual review form, which was required by the department to evaluate the progress of graduate students from the viewpoint of their advisor. I had the toughest conversation with my advisor that day, and it led me to examine the importance of the advisor?advisee relationship. I talked to many faculty members and graduate students about their experiences regarding this issue after that meeting. Little by little, I noticed that the main reason for that tough conversation was my advisor's concerns about my success, but it was hard for me to understand that in the beginning.

articleTitle: Orbital Mechanics for the Young Science Fiction Villain
abstract: Orbits occur when an object is moving fast enough, but not too fast, relative to a central body that gravity pulls its trajectory into an ellipse . Too slow, and gravity pulls the mass into a collision course. Too much velocity behind the mass, and it will overcome the acceleration (pull) of gravity to continue onward, uninterrupted, "To infinity and beyond!". Something to keep in mind when talking about orbital mechanics is that Sir Isaac Newton invented calculus just so he could talk about it intelligently with math.

articleTitle: Ultrasound Elastography Probe Design for Diagnosing Rotator Cuff Pathology
abstract: The shoulder is a complex and dynamic joint that offers the widest range of motion of any joint in the human body. With this incredible mobility comes inherent instability due to the lack of bony constraint. The shoulder is dynamically stabilized through the rotator cuff, a group of muscles that act synergistically throughout the range of motion. These muscles include the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, and subscapularis (Fig. 1). Unfortunately, they are prone to tearing near their tendinous insertions, generally due to age-related degenerative changes, trauma, subacromial impingement, and repetitive stresses. Injury to the rotator cuff accounts for nearly 50% of all major shoulder injuries and is highly prevalent in people aged 60 years or older (Murrell and Walton, 2001).

articleTitle: The Advent of Data Science Platforms
abstract: As a reader of IEEE Potentials, you are very likely an undergraduate or graduate student who likes technology. There is a good chance that you are reading this article on your smartphone, that little electrical device that you can hold in a pocket. The device is quite common, considering that about 40% of the worldwide population has one (O'Dea, 2020).

articleTitle: Johnny Still Can't Write! [Chasing Rays]
abstract: Some years ago, I wrote an article for the IEEE Professional Communications Society newsletter. The title of the article was "...but Johnny can't write!" The article looked at a problem experienced by undergraduate engineers entering their new career in industry. Simply put, they couldn't write to the level expected of college graduates. One would expect to see a marked improvement over the intervening years, but that is not what is happening.

articleTitle: Students Interested in Making Money Should Not Skip School
abstract: Many students are dropping out of their universities. A few have become billionaires. (The best example of this is Bill Gates.) Where should students go to earn money? The answer is that they should go to a place where they can learn something. Therefore, students interested in making money should go to school. Knowledge can be gained in school; then, money can be earned.

articleTitle: Making Your Conference Visit Worthwhile
abstract: Regardless of whether you are a student, researcher, or early career faculty member, as long as you are in academia, attending conferences is inevitable. I wrote more than 20 conference publications while I was a graduate student at the University of Colorado Denver and as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Saskatchewan, Saskatoon, Canada. Because I like traveling, conferences never bothered me. But that might not be the opinion you hear from everybody. One general question is, how does one get the most out of a conference? The answers to that question vary The following are some tips that I Ashanthi Maxworth have learned over the years that might help you decide if is it worth attending conferences and how to get the best out of them.

articleTitle: To Infinity and Beyond
abstract: There is something mesmerizing about space that has captivated humanity for generations and inspired artists, scientists, and engineers alike. However, it was not until the late 1950s that humans were able to design and build a rocket capable of breaking through the force of gravity to reach space. Early on, most space activities were carried out by the governments from a few nations; in recent years, we have seen many commercial and educational initiatives that are making space more accessible to everyone. This issue of IEEE Potentials is dedicated to topics of space exploration, highlighting projects and ideas fueling the current and future generations of explorers.

articleTitle: Industry or Academia: Where Are the Innovators?
abstract: Where are the innovators? The answer to this question is complex; as an immediate response, one might answer, "It depends!" To begin with, it is appropriate to define two words that frequently cross each other in such discussions? innovation and research. Innovation has two common definitions: 1) a new idea, device, or method and 2) the act or process of introducing new ideas, devices, or methods. In contrast, research is defined as the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources to establish facts and reach new conclusions.

articleTitle: Don't Plagiarize-Recognize
abstract: In simplest terms, plagiarism is the use of someone else's intellectual property as if it were your own personally developed concept. This can be something as simple as a few words to pictures, large blocks of text, charts, and other similar material. In short, if someone else developed the information, it is not free to be used without recognizing that source. In some instances, formal release may be required for such use.

articleTitle: Self-Driving Vehicles: Key Technical Challenges and Progress Off the Road
abstract: In a period of fewer than 10 years, the quest for self-driving vehicles, also referred to as autonomous vehicles (AVs) or driverless cars, has become one of the biggest technology races in the world, with tens of billions of dollars poured into companies and start-ups. The goal is an on-road, consumer-driverless car: whether owned by individuals or part of a centralized ride-sharing fleet, this is the area where the majority of investment has occurred. However, AVs have been around for much longer in other fields, such as mining, which share some but not all of the same technical challenges faced by on-road AVs. In this article, we provide an overview of the key technical challenges and solutions for both onand off-road AVs, with a focus on one of the key unsolved challenges-interaction with vulnerable road users (VRUs).

articleTitle: ManitobaSat-1: A Novel Approach for Technology Advancement
abstract: ManitobaSat-1 is a 3U CubeSat program that is determined to advance the edges of space technology by performing things differently from traditional design strategies (see Fig.1). This will enhance access to space through novel technology development and verification and enable smaller companies to benefit from satellite services. ManitobaSat-1 is being developed at the University of Manitoba by the Space Technologies and Advanced Research Laboratory (STARLab) in collaboration with the Center for Terrestrial and Planetary Exploration at the University of Winnipeg, York University, the Interlake School Division, and Magellan Aerospace, our industrial partner.

articleTitle: A Peer-Mentoring Experience for Graduate Students
abstract: A mentor is someone who provides guidance, assistance, and support to a less-experienced individual. The individual, a mentee, is a person who benefits from the guidance and assistance by learning from those who walked a similar path before him or her. In the context of graduate studies, an advisor?student relationship is consistent with this description.

articleTitle: Enabling Commercial Autonomous Robotic Space Explorers
abstract: In contrast to sending humans to explore space, the application of autonomous robots reduces safety concerns and extends the possible mission distance since return transportation is not necessary. In addition, the use of robots decreases complexities and costs because there is no need for onboard life-support systems; robots can withstand and operate in harsh conditions, such as extreme temperature, pressure, and radiation, where humans cannot survive.

abstract: Advertisement: We have 30 million reasons to be proud. Realize Your ImpactLearn how: ieeefoundation.org/campaignThanks to our donors, supporters and volunteers who answered the call of the Realize the Full Potential of IEEE Campaign, helping impact lives around the world through the power of technology and education.

articleTitle: You Can Be the Next Student Editor of IEEE Potentials!
abstract: Advertisement, IEEE.

articleTitle: Bid Data: An Engineering Marvel [Editorial]
abstract: Presents the introductory editorial for this issue of the publication.

articleTitle: Leadership in Uncertain Times [The Way Ahead]
abstract: One of my favorite movies is Apollo 13. An oxygen tank fails two days into the mission as the spacecraft heads to the moon, and the astronauts have to put together an alternative mechanism to propel their ship back to Earth and provide them with enough oxygen to survive the trip. I love when a manager drops a box of all of the materials that are on board the spaceship on a table in front of a team of engineers in Houston, telling them to find a solution. I think that really describes what engineers do: we solve problems in the context of external constraints. This is such a foundational part of being an engineer that the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology, which accredits most U.S. (and many international) engineering programs, requires that programs show the board how what we teach you helps you to learn to solve problems given constraints. We don’t ask you to solve problems such as those you see in Apollo 13, but you should recognize that theme in multiple places in your program.

articleTitle: Have a Personal Mission and Vision [The Way Ahead]
abstract: Do you have a vision? This issue of IEEE Potentials is about medical technology. I want to consider vision as a concept that encompasses more than just the physical ability to see or technology that helps with physical vision. Most organizations have mission and vision statements. A mission statement defines the organization’s business, its objectives, and its approach to reaching those objectives, whereas a vision statement describes the desired future position of the organization. The mission statement describes what you want to do now, and the vision statement outlines what you want to be in the future. The IEEE’s mission statement is “IEEE’s core purpose is to foster technological innovation and excellence for the benefit of humanity.”

articleTitle: Beyond Technological Boundaries [Editorial]
abstract: Presents the introductory editoral for this issue of the publication.

articleTitle: The Importance of Community [Editorial]
abstract: Presents the introductory editorial for this issue of the publication.

articleTitle: Preparing for a Career That You Cannot Envision [The Way Ahead]
abstract: For my column in IEEE Potentials careers and graduate education theme issue last year, I shared common questions employers ask references when considering future employees. This year, the world has changed a bit. Employers are still hiring high-tech workers, so most IEEE Student Members are in a much better situation than many of their fellow citizens. Still, numerous companies are slowing down their hiring. Many students lost the summer internships they had been counting on. Students and recent graduates are reevaluating the job landscape.

articleTitle: Invent the Future [The Way Ahead]
abstract: Reports on new areas of new areas of technological development for the future.

articleTitle: The International Journey of a Medical Technology Student [Tech Travel]
abstract: In this “Tech Travel” column, IEEE Potentials Editorial Board members Cátia Bandeiras and Mahshid Iraniparast discuss their international journeys as medical technology (MedTech) students and how the IEEE shaped their careers in the field. Both women are originally from Region 8 and did their graduate studies in the United States.

articleTitle: Student Congresses [The Way Ahead]
abstract: Presents information on IEEE Regional activities.

articleTitle: In Community, We Find Our Strength [Editorial]
abstract: Presents the introductory editorial for this issue of the publication.

articleTitle: The Path of the Tapir [Editorial]
abstract: Presents the introductory editorial for this issue of the publication.

articleTitle: Building a Better Blogger
abstract: Jacquelyn Adams began her training career teaching high school math in Swahili in a rural Tanzanian village for two years as a Peace Corps volunteer. Upon returning to the United States, she combined her love of teaching with her B.S. degree in computer engineering to become a corporate engineering trainer. After spending a decade as a top-rated instructor, she founded a consulting company, Ristole. Adams is an IEEE Senior Member and serves as the vice chair of both the IEEE's Continuing Education Committee and Public Visibility Committee. She has received local and national recognition for her professional achievements. including Top 40 Under 40, Entrepreneurial Achievement, Outstanding Young Alumni, and Outstanding Woman in Business awards. Her blog, Lessons on Leadership (https://insight.ieeeusa.org/jacquelyn-adams/), shares leadership development tips and has become the most read column on IEEE-USA InSight. Adams also hosts the IEEE.tv channel Jacquelyn Worx, which focuses on the future of work and career development.

abstract: Presents the introductory editorial for this issue of the publication

articleTitle: When Pursuing a Ph.D. Degree
abstract: Every work needs inspiration, and so, too, does pursuing a Ph.D. degree. However, a problem occurs when most of the scholars studying for a doctorate are doing so only to hold another degree or obtain higher title. The "why" to obtain a Ph.D. degree should focus on research, as most doctoral candidates will be in either academia or industry research-not something a general engineering student will pursue.
